title: Week 6 Mastery Quiz — Belief, Ethics, and Philosophy

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes dharma in the context of this course?
choices: A single rule identical in every South Asian tradition
A Chinese term for family responsibility
A complex concept involving duty, order, conduct, and right living
A synonym for monotheism
questions.explanation: Dharma is a complex South Asian concept whose meanings vary by context and tradition.

choices: A political office in ancient China
A covenant between a ruler and subjects
A term meaning belief in one God
A principle concerning the moral consequences of actions, interpreted in varied ways across South Asian traditions
questions.explanation: Karma concerns actions and their consequences; traditions differ in how they explain its operation.

questions.prompt: In Buddhist traditions, nirvana refers most directly to:
choices: liberation from craving, suffering, and the cycle of rebirth
obedience to a hereditary ruler
family lineage worship
a written legal code
questions.explanation: Nirvana refers to liberation, not a political office, family practice, or law code.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest historical caution when reading a sacred or philosophical text?
choices: Religious texts cannot be historical evidence.
Genre, translation, audience, historical setting, and later interpretation affect what claims the text can support.
A translated passage always preserves every nuance of its earliest form.
One passage represents every believer across all periods.
questions.explanation: Context and transmission matter, and one text cannot automatically represent all practitioners or periods.

questions.prompt: Filial piety in Confucian thought most directly concerns:
choices: liberation from rebirth
belief in one God
responsibilities and respect within family relationships
the spread of cultural traits through trade
questions.explanation: Filial piety concerns family relationships and responsibilities within Confucian ethical thought.

questions.prompt: Why is the statement “all religions teach the same thing” historically inadequate?
choices: No traditions ever address similar questions.
Only philosophical traditions change over time.
Comparison between traditions is impossible.
Shared questions or ethical concerns can coexist with major differences in concepts, practices, texts, institutions, and historical development.
questions.explanation: Responsible comparison recognizes genuine similarities without erasing meaningful differences.

questions.prompt: Which approach best reflects academic study of religion in a social studies classroom?
choices: Describe and analyze beliefs, practices, sources, and historical effects without requiring acceptance or rejection of a faith.
Ask students to decide which tradition is true.
Treat sacred texts as slogans detached from context.
Assume rulers always practiced the ideals found in religious texts.
questions.explanation: Academic study analyzes religion historically and respectfully without devotional endorsement or rejection.

questions.prompt: A Confucian text describes the conduct of an ideal ruler. What can a historian conclude most safely?
choices: Every Chinese ruler behaved exactly that way.
The passage provides evidence about an articulated ideal; actual political practice requires additional evidence.
The passage proves ordinary people supported the government.
The ideal had no historical influence.
questions.explanation: Normative texts reveal ideals, but practice must be investigated through corroborating evidence.

choices: Match vocabulary words that sound similar and assume the concepts are identical.
Rank traditions according to which is most rational.
Compare how two traditions address a clearly defined question, use contextualized evidence, and explain both similarity and difference.
Use one modern practitioner to represent an entire tradition across history.
questions.explanation: A bounded question, contextualized evidence, and attention to both similarity and difference produce stronger comparison.

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarizes the historical relationship between belief systems and society?
choices: Beliefs determine social institutions in exactly the same way everywhere.
Belief systems affect only private worship.
Political rulers never reinterpret ethical traditions.
Religious and philosophical traditions can influence law, family, education, legitimacy, art, and reform, while interpretation and practice vary across communities and time.
questions.explanation: Traditions can have broad social influence, but their meanings and applications vary historically.

shortResponse.prompt: Using contextualized evidence from at least three traditions studied in Week 6, compare how people addressed one shared question—duty, suffering, justice, identity, or good government. Explain at least one important difference and one limitation of the surviving evidence.
shortResponse.exemplar: Full-credit work frames one clear comparative question, uses accurate contextualized evidence from at least three traditions, explains a meaningful difference rather than flattening the traditions, and identifies an evidentiary limitation or interpretive caution.
